question: In the Indian Constitution the "Financial Emergency" is mentioned in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 360**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Financial Emergency is mentioned under **Article 360** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The President of India has the authority to declare a Financial Emergency if there is a threat to the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory.
 
• During a Financial Emergency, the executive authority of the Union extends to giving directions to any state to observe financial propriety.
 
• The salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving in the Union or State may be reduced during the period of Financial Emergency.
 
• Article 360 has never been invoked in India since the adoption of the Constitution in 1950.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Emergency (Article 352):**

 
 
• Declared during war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• It leads to the centralization of power and can alter the federal structure of the country temporarily.
 
 
 
• **President’s Rule (Article 356):**
 
 
• Declared when there is a failure of constitutional machinery in a state.
 
• The state government is suspended, and the President administers the state directly through the Governor.
 
 
 
• **Financial Emergency Provisions:**
 
 
• Parliament can modify the distribution of financial resources between the Union and States during a Financial Emergency.
 
• It ensures that the financial stability of the country is maintained.
 
 
 
• **Comparison:**
 
 
• While National and President's Rule have been invoked multiple times, Financial Emergency remains unused in India.
 
• This reflects the strength and resilience of India's financial system.
